descriptionChirho: To take possession of or occupy territory, especially the promised land, by entering and settling it (Arabic: امتلك imtalaka / وَرِثَ waritha in territorial context; Korean: 차지하다 chajihada; Swahili: -miliki; Hindi: अधिकार करना).

To receive as an inheritance or heritage, especially in family succession or covenant blessing (Arabic: يَرِثُ yarithu; Korean: 상속하다 sangsok-hada / 유업하다; Swahili: -rithi; Hindi: वारिस होना / विरासत में लेना).

To dispossess or drive out people from their land, taking their place (Qal with personal object; Arabic: طَرَدُوهُمْ taraduhum = expelled them; Korean: 멸망시키다 / 빼앗다; Swahili: -rithi in displacement sense; Hindi: उजाड़ना).
One who inherits or possesses, an heir or rightful owner (nominalized Qal participle; Arabic: وَارِث warith; Korean: 상속자 sangsokja; Swahili: mrithi; Hindi: वारिस / उत्तराधिकारी).
To drive out or dispossess inhabitants from their land by force (causative; Arabic: طَرَدَ tarada = expel; Korean: 쫓아내다 jjochaneda; Swahili: -fukuza; Hindi: निकालना).

labelChirho: Hifil: cause to inherit or bequeath
descriptionChirho: To give someone an inheritance or grant possession of territory as a gift or bequest (causative of inheritance; Arabic: أَوْرَثَ awratha / يُوَرِّثُ yuwarrithu; Korean: 물려주다 / 유산으로 주다; Swahili: -rithisha; Hindi: विरासत में देना).
To become poor, be reduced to poverty, or be dispossessed of one's wealth (passive/reflexive; Arabic: يَفْتَقِرُ yaftaqiru = become destitute; Korean: 가난해지다; Swahili: kuwa maskini; Hindi: गरीब होना).
To cause someone to become poor, to reduce to poverty (causative of becoming poor; Arabic: يُفْقِرُ yufqiru = makes poor; Korean: 가난하게 하다; Swahili: anafanya maskini; Hindi: गरीब करना).
To take firm possession of something (intensive/factitive; Arabic: يَمْتَلِكُهُ yamtalikuhu; Korean: 차지하리라; Swahili: atamiliki; Hindi: अधिकार करना).
